label: Potential friend count
summary: Whether the number of potential friends the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the potential friend type. Compare it with a number, for example `> 0`. The game's documentation gives no more detail, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Potential hook count
summary: Whether the number of potential hook relations the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the potential hook type. Compare it with a number, for example `> 0`. The game's documentation gives no more detail, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Potential lover count
summary: Whether the number of potential lovers the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the potential lover type. Compare it with a number, for example `> 0`. The game's documentation gives no more detail, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Potential rival count
summary: Whether the number of potential rivals the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the potential rival type. Compare it with a number, for example `> 0`. The game's documentation gives no more detail, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Rival count
summary: Whether the number of rivals the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the rival type. Vanilla mostly compares with `< 2` (12 of 18 uses). Other uses are `>= 1`, `>= 2`, `>= 4` and `<= 2`.

label: Soldier friend count
summary: Whether the number of soldier friends the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the soldier friend type. Vanilla uses it once, checking for exactly 0.

label: Soulmate count
summary: Whether the number of soulmates the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the soulmate type. Vanilla mostly uses it to check that the character has none (`0` or `<= 0`) and once checks for 1.

label: Student count
summary: Whether the number of students the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the student type. Compare it with a number, for example `> 0`. The game's documentation gives no more detail, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Victim count
summary: Whether the number of victims the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the victim type. Vanilla uses it once, checking that there are none (`<= 0`).

label: Ward count
summary: Whether the number of wards the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the ward type. Vanilla nearly always compares with `< 2` (40 of 46 uses); the other uses are `>= 2`, `<= 1` and `> 1`.

label: Bad fertility wedding count
summary: Whether the number of bad fertility wedding relations the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the wedding bad fertility type. Compare it with a number. The game's documentation gives no more detail, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Good fertility wedding count
summary: Whether the number of good fertility wedding relations the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the wedding good fertility type. Compare it with a number. The game's documentation gives no more detail, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Very bad fertility wedding count
summary: Whether the number of very bad fertility wedding relations the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the wedding very bad fertility type. Compare it with a number. The game's documentation gives no more detail, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Very good fertility wedding count
summary: Whether the number of very good fertility wedding relations the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the wedding very good fertility type. Compare it with a number. The game's documentation gives no more detail, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Wet nurse count
summary: Whether the number of wet nurse relations the character has meets a comparison.
details: It counts the character's scripted relations of the wet nurse type. Compare it with a number, for example `> 0`. The game's documentation gives no more detail, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Offered task contracts
summary: Whether the number of task contracts the character currently offers meets a comparison.
details: The game's documentation says it counts the active task contracts the character has offered. Its example is `scope:actor = { num_offered_task_contracts > 0 }`. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Travel options chosen
summary: Whether the number of travel options selected for the travel plan meets a comparison.
details: It works on a travel plan. The game's documentation gives no more detail, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Past activity phases
summary: Whether the number of phases of the activity that are already over meets a comparison.
details: It works on an activity. Vanilla uses it once, with `>= 1`, so it asks whether at least one phase has passed.

label: Personal legend seeds
summary: Whether the number of personal legend seeds available to the character meets a comparison.
details: Vanilla uses it twice, both times with `>= 1`.

label: Activity phases
summary: Whether the total number of phases planned for the activity meets a comparison.
details: The game's documentation says it counts the phases planned for the activity. It works on an activity. Vanilla compares it with values from 2 to 5, either exactly or with `>`.

label: Rite character followers
summary: Whether the number of characters that follow the rite meets a comparison.
details: It works on a rite. The game's documentation says it counts characters following "the given faith", but the trigger works on a rite and vanilla does not use it, so the exact meaning is unclear.

label: Rite county followers
summary: Whether the number of counties that follow the rite meets a comparison.
details: It works on a rite. Vanilla uses it three times, with `> 0`, `>= 3` and `>= 40`.

label: Scripted legend seeds
summary: Whether the number of scripted legend seeds available to the character meets a comparison.
details: It counts seeds whether or not they are currently valid to start. Compare it with `num_triggered_legend_seeds`, which counts only the valid ones. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Sinful traits
summary: Whether the number of traits the character has that a rite counts as sinful meets a comparison.
details: Written as a plain comparison, it uses the character's own rite. Written as a block, `target` picks another rite to judge by. Vanilla mostly writes `>= 1` or `> 0`, and the block form with `target = faith.main_rite`.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison for the number of sinful traits.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The rite that decides which traits count as sinful.

label: Taken task contracts
summary: Whether the number of task contracts the character has accepted and not yet finished meets a comparison.
details: The documented example is `scope:actor = { num_taken_task_contracts > 0 }`. Vanilla uses it twice, to check that there are none.

label: Task contracts
summary: Whether the number of task contracts the character has meets a comparison.
details: The documented example is `scope:actor = { num_task_contracts > 0 }`. The game's documentation does not say which contracts it counts; the related triggers count offered and taken ones. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Total troops in combat
summary: Whether the total number of troops on both sides of the combat meets a comparison.
details: It works on a combat and counts the troops of both sides together. Vanilla compares it with large numbers such as `>= 20000`. Two other vanilla uses are blocks with `add` and `multiply` instead of a comparison; the input does not show what those do.

label: Triggered legend seeds
summary: Whether the number of legend seeds available to the character that are also valid to start meets a comparison.
details: Compare it with `num_scripted_legend_seeds`, which counts the seeds whether or not they are valid. Vanilla uses it twice, both times with `>= 1`.

label: Virtuous traits
summary: Whether the number of traits the character has that a rite counts as virtuous meets a comparison.
details: Written as a plain comparison, it uses the character's own rite. Written as a block, `target` picks another rite to judge by. The value can be another trigger's count, as in `> num_sinful_traits`.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison for the number of virtuous traits.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The rite that decides which traits count as virtuous.

label: Men-at-arms regiments of base type
summary: Whether the character has the given number of men-at-arms regiments of a base type.
details: It counts regiments, not single soldiers. Vanilla uses base types such as archers, pikemen and light cavalry.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The base type of men-at-arms to count.
fields.values: a base type such as `archers`, `pikemen` or `light_cavalry`

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison for the number of regiments.

label: Men-at-arms regiments of type
summary: Whether the character has the given number of men-at-arms regiments of one specific type.
details: It counts regiments, not single soldiers. The game's documentation shows no usage, and vanilla does not use it, so the fields are unknown. The similar `number_maa_regiments_of_base_type` takes `type` and `value`.

label: Men-at-arms soldiers of base type
summary: Whether the character has the given number of soldiers in men-at-arms regiments of a base type.
details: It counts single soldiers, not regiments. Vanilla uses it with values such as `>= 500` for skirmishers or archers.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The base type of men-at-arms to count.
fields.values: a base type such as `skirmishers`, `archers` or `heavy_cavalry`

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison for the number of soldiers.

label: Men-at-arms soldiers of type
summary: Whether the character has the given number of soldiers in men-at-arms regiments of one specific type.
details: It counts single soldiers. The game's documentation shows no usage; the one vanilla use writes `target = varangian_guards` next to `value`, so the field names are taken from that single use.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison for the number of soldiers.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The men-at-arms type to count, as written in vanilla's single use.

label: Characters in pool
summary: Whether the number of characters in the character pool that the province belongs to meets a comparison.
details: It works on a province, and counts the pool the province is part of. Vanilla uses it once, comparing with a value that stands for a full pool (`>= full_pool_size`).

label: Commander traits
summary: Whether the number of commander traits the character has meets a comparison.
details: Vanilla mostly compares with `< 3` (36 of 78 uses) or `< commander_trait_limit`, so it is mostly used to check that the character is below a limit.

label: Shared commander traits
summary: Whether the character and a target share the given number of commander traits.
details: Vanilla uses it twice with `target = root` and `value < 1`, which checks that they share none. The documented usage line names a different trigger (`number_of_personality_traits_in_common`), a copy slip that the vanilla block fields confirm.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison for the number of shared traits.

label: Concubines
summary: Whether the number of concubines the character has meets a comparison.
details: Vanilla checks for none (`0`), for at least one (`> 0`), or for fewer than a limit it names, such as `< number_of_desired_concubines`.

label: Desired concubines
summary: Whether the number of fertile concubines the character should have to avoid penalties meets a comparison.
details: The game's documentation says it is the number of fertile concubines the character should have to avoid penalties, not the number they have. Compare it with `number_of_concubines`. Vanilla does not use it as a trigger; it appears only as a comparison value.

label: Election votes
summary: Whether the number of votes the character has in an election for the target title meets a comparison.
details: It is written as a block. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: title
fields.text: The title whose election is checked.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison for the number of votes.

label: Faction members in council
summary: Whether the number of faction members that sit in the council meets a comparison.
details: It works on a faction. The game's documentation calls it the current number of faction members in the faction, which is not quite the same as in the council, so the exact meaning is unclear. Vanilla does not use it.
